title: feat: pipe block tables with arrow markers
description:
## What
Parse contiguous blocks of pipe-separated lines as tables. Arrow markers on column headers determine which columns generate cards and in which direction. Cards have a two-line front with context derived from the column headers.

## Syntax
```
subject | conjugation <->
yo | soy
tú | eres
él/ella | es
```

Arrow markers on header cells:
- `col <->` — bidirectional (row ↔ cell)
- `col ->` — forward only (row → cell)
- `col <-` — backward only (cell → row)
- no arrow — display only, no cards generated

Empty trailing cells are valid (missing values, no card generated for that cell).

## Context
Context always comes from the column headers, joined as `<subject col> → <value col>`. No heading lookup.

## Card output
Cards have a two-line front with context on line 1:

- Forward: `<subject col> → <value col>` / `<row value> →?` — back: `<cell value>`
- Reverse: `<subject col> → <value col>` / `? ← <cell value>` — back: `<row value>`

Example with `<->` column:
- Forward: line 1 `subject → conjugation` / line 2 `yo →?` — back `soy`
- Reverse: line 1 `subject → conjugation` / line 2 `? ← soy` — back `yo`

## Work required
- Disable pulldown-cmark GFM tables (already off) and implement a custom block-detection pass over raw text, OR add a pre-parse line scan to detect pipe-block groups before feeding to cmark
- Parse the first line to extract column headers + their arrow markers; strip markers from the display name
- For each data row, for each marked column, emit the appropriate card(s) with two-line fronts:
  - Forward: `"{subject col} → {value col}\n{row value} →?"` / `"{cell value}"`
  - Reverse: `"{subject col} → {value col}\n? ← {cell value}"` / `"{row value}"`
- Handle empty trailing cells (skip card generation for that cell)
- Add unit tests in `doc-parser/tests/examples.rs`
- Add integration tests in `acli/tests/integration.rs`

## Files
- `doc-parser/src/parser.rs` (new block-detection pass)
- `doc-parser/src/types.rs` (may reuse existing CardType variants)
- `doc-parser/tests/examples.rs`
- `acli/tests/integration.rs`

title: feat: attribute cards (heading + key -> value bullets)
description:
## What
Track the nearest preceding Markdown heading as a subject label and apply it as a prefix on question fields for `key -> value` list items beneath it.

## Syntax
```
# Hydrogen
- symbol -> H
- atomic number -> 1
- phase -> gas
```

## Card output
Each bullet generates a card with a two-line front:

- Front line 1: `<subject>` (e.g. `Hydrogen`)
- Front line 2: `<key> →?` (e.g. `symbol →?`)
- Back: `<value>` (e.g. `H`)

If no heading precedes the bullet, it is treated as a plain basic card — not an attribute card with silently dropped context.

## Work required
- Track current heading text in `ParseState` in `doc-parser/src/parser.rs` (handle `Start(Tag::Heading)` events currently falling through to `_ => None`)
- When generating a card from a leaf list item, if a heading context is set, build the front field as `"{Heading}\n{question} →?"` (newline-separated)
- If no heading context is set, emit a plain basic card instead
- Decide scoping: does a new heading clear the previous? (yes — each heading resets the subject)
- Add unit tests in `doc-parser/tests/examples.rs`
- Add integration tests in `acli/tests/integration.rs`

## Files
- `doc-parser/src/parser.rs` (ParseState + card generation)
- `doc-parser/tests/examples.rs`
- `acli/tests/integration.rs`

title: Fix main.rs to use anyhow::Result instead of process::exit
description:
**Background**: Rust skill prescribes app binaries use `anyhow` for error handling — `fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()>` and propagate with `?` + `.context()`. The `acli` binary currently defines a `CliError` thiserror enum used pervasively across the binary crate, and `main.rs` uses `eprintln!` + `process::exit`.

**Current state**: `CliError` (thiserror) is used in: `cli.rs`, `sync.rs`, `config.rs`, `discovery.rs`, `error.rs`. All internal functions return `Result<_, CliError>`. `main.rs` calls `run()` and manually handles the error with eprintln + exit.

**Goal**: Remove the `CliError` thiserror enum entirely. All binary-internal functions use `anyhow::Result<T>`. Error context added with `.context("...")" at call sites. `main.rs` becomes `fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()>`.

**Constraints**: Library crates (doc-parser, anki-wrapper, web-preview) keep their typed errors — only the `acli` binary crate changes. User-visible error messages must remain clear. `cargo build && rtk cargo test` must pass.

**Checklist**:
- [ ] Add `anyhow = "1"` to `acli/Cargo.toml`, remove `thiserror`
- [ ] Delete `acli/src/error.rs` (CliError enum)
- [ ] Update `config.rs` to return `anyhow::Result`, replace `CliError::` constructors with `.context()`
- [ ] Update `discovery.rs` similarly
- [ ] Update `sync.rs` similarly
- [ ] Update `cli.rs` similarly (largest file — most `CliError` usages)
- [ ] Change `main.rs` to `fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()>`
- [ ] Verify: `cargo build && rtk cargo test`

title: feat: ordered sequence cards (=> prefix)
description:
## What
Parse lines prefixed with `=>` as ordered sequences that generate a chain of cards. A required plain-text label line immediately above the block provides context for all cards in the sequence.

## Syntax
```
Troubleshoot Wi-Fi connection
=> check Wi-Fi is enabled
=> restart device
=> forget network and reconnect
```

The plain-text line directly above the first `=>` is the label. It is required.

## Card output
Each card has a two-line front with the label on line 1:

- First item — front: `<label>` / `First:` — back: `<first step>`
- Each subsequent item — front: `<label>` / `After: <previous step>` — back: `<next step>`

## Work required
- Add `CardType::Sequence` (or equivalent) variant to `doc-parser/src/types.rs`
- Detect a plain-text label line immediately above a contiguous `=>`-prefixed block in `doc-parser/src/parser.rs`
- Emit the correct sequence of cards with two-line fronts (`"<label>\nFirst:"` / `"<label>\nAfter: <prev step>"`)
- Wire new CardType through `acli/src/adapter.rs` to Anki (Basic note type, two fields)
- Add unit tests in `doc-parser/tests/examples.rs` and integration tests in `acli/tests/integration.rs`

## Files
- `doc-parser/src/types.rs`
- `doc-parser/src/parser.rs`
- `acli/src/adapter.rs`

title: Rewrite MarkdownParser::parse() using pulldown-cmark AST
description: Replace the line-based parser with a pulldown-cmark event walker. **File:** doc-parser/src/parser.rs pulldown-cmark v0.9 is already declared as a dependency but unused. The current parser is ~120 lines of manual line splitting. Rewrite to walk the pulldown-cmark event stream: 1. Track list nesting depth via Start(List)/End(List) and Start(Item)/End(Item) events 2. Within each list item, accumulate inline content (text, images, emphasis, etc.) 3. Scan accumulated text for -> or <-> arrow delimiters to split into question/answer 4. Extract raw text for each side (preserving inline formatting as-is) 5. Replace image syntax with tags 6. Non-leaf items (those containing sub-lists) become context parents **Key design point:** Arrow detection happens on the text content of a list item. Card fields remain as raw text (same as today), except that ![alt](path) image syntax gets replaced with tags. Existing text-only cards produce identical Card.fields and identical CardId hashes. **Tests (must pass all existing tests with identical output):** - test_basic_card — "One -> 1" → fields ["One -> ?", "1"] (unchanged) - test_bidirectional_card — "One <-> 1" → fields ["One <-> ?", "1"] (unchanged) - test_nested_context_list — parent context propagation (unchanged) **New tests:** - Arrow inside code span is NOT treated as delimiter - Inline formatting preserved as-is in fields See: notes/image-support-plan.md (Task 0.1)
